periods.analysis: Harborview starts this series in a strong prevention position: Primary Care Access Rate is 87.6%, above the >=85 target, and Restaurant Inspection Compliance is 93.6%, above the >=92 target. Because this is our baseline quarter, the important fact is not movement yet but margin: both measures have enough cushion to absorb normal seasonal pressure without losing green status. The North Clinic same-week cohort, the South Harbor mobile intake route, and the food safety team’s Friday reinspection block all appear to be contributing to steady access and safer dining environments. Clinically, these are upstream results: people are getting routine care before conditions worsen, and food establishments are correcting risks before residents become ill.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the same-week appointment model at North Clinic and extend the South Harbor mobile intake route to two additional senior housing stops in October. Keep the Friday reinspection block for restaurants with critical-item corrections, and add a brief pre-holiday operator bulletin on cooling logs, shellfish tags, and handwashing compliance. Use 2024-Q3 as the operating baseline for access and inspection scheduling through the next two quarters.

periods.analysis: Primary Care Access Rate eased from 87.6% to 86.8%, a quarter-over-quarter decrease of 0.8 percentage points, but it remains above the >=85 target. Restaurant Inspection Compliance improved from 93.6% to 93.8%, a quarter-over-quarter increase of 0.2 percentage points, also remaining above the >=92 target. The access dip is consistent with year-end respiratory illness volume and holiday staffing gaps, especially at the Bayside and Maple urgent-primary care panels. The inspection gain suggests the Environmental Health unit’s recheck cadence worked even as winter events increased restaurant volume along Pier Avenue.
periods.recommendations: Maintain green performance by protecting four same-day respiratory slots per provider at Bayside and Maple from mid-November through January. Extend the food safety recheck cadence to all Pier Avenue and Boardwalk establishments with prior temperature-control findings. Review no-show data by language preference and appointment type so the access margin does not narrow further in winter.

periods.analysis: Primary Care Access Rate rose from 86.8% to 87.3%, a quarter-over-quarter increase of 0.5 percentage points, returning some of the winter access margin. Restaurant Inspection Compliance moved from 93.8% to 93.6%, a quarter-over-quarter decrease of 0.2 percentage points, but remained comfortably above the >=92 target. The care access recovery tracks with the January launch of text-confirmation workflows for the Harborview Community Health Network and the addition of Tuesday evening nurse triage at Westport Clinic. The small inspection decline was concentrated in new food trucks and pop-up vendors entering the spring permit cycle, not in long-standing high-volume restaurants.
periods.recommendations: Continue the text-confirmation workflow and expand it to dental-medical referral visits, where missed appointments still create preventable delays. Assign Environmental Health Specialist Team B to a March orientation session for new food trucks and pop-up vendors before festival season begins. Keep measuring access by neighborhood cohort so citywide green status does not hide a pocket of delayed care.

periods.analysis: This quarter shows clear operational lift: Primary Care Access Rate increased from 87.3% to 89%, a quarter-over-quarter increase of 1.7 percentage points. Restaurant Inspection Compliance increased from 93.6% to 95.6%, a quarter-over-quarter increase of 2.0 percentage points, widening the margin above the >=92 target. The improvement aligns with the CareFirst scheduling template, which reserved early-week preventive visit blocks, and with the Environmental Health unit’s Route 4 paired-inspector model for waterfront restaurants. From a population-health view, this is the right direction: better access supports immunizations, screenings, and chronic disease control, while stronger inspection compliance reduces avoidable foodborne illness risk.
periods.recommendations: Lock in the CareFirst template for another quarter and add one Saturday preventive-care clinic each month at South Harbor for workers who cannot attend weekday visits. Keep Route 4 paired inspections through the summer tourism peak and use the same model for high-volume seafood and commissary kitchens. Publish a short dashboard for clinic managers showing weekly third-next-available appointment trends so the 89% access rate is sustained.

periods.analysis: Primary Care Access Rate decreased from 89% to 88%, a quarter-over-quarter decrease of 1.0 percentage point, but it remains above the >=85 target. Restaurant Inspection Compliance decreased from 95.6% to 94.5%, a quarter-over-quarter decrease of 1.1 percentage points, still above the >=92 target. The softening is expected after a very strong Q2 and during Harborview’s summer surge, when temporary food permits, visitor volume, and provider vacations all stress the system. Green status is appropriate, but the prevention lesson is clear: summer demand needs planned capacity, not heroic catch-up in September.
periods.recommendations: Pre-book summer backfill for primary care panels by May next year, using per-diem nurse practitioners for the Bayside, Westport, and South Harbor clinics. For restaurants, continue temporary-event permit huddles at the marina office every Monday during peak season and require same-week correction photos for low-risk structural findings. Maintain the Saturday preventive-care clinic and compare attendance by ZIP code before deciding whether to add a second monthly session.

periods.analysis: Primary Care Access Rate improved from 88% to 88.3%, a quarter-over-quarter increase of 0.3 percentage points, keeping access solidly above the >=85 target. Restaurant Inspection Compliance decreased from 94.5% to 93.5%, a quarter-over-quarter decrease of 1.0 percentage point, but remains above the >=92 target. The access gain indicates the fall panel-balancing work helped, particularly the redistribution of 1,200 low-acuity patients from the overfull Maple panel to Harborview Family Practice. The inspection decline is watchable but not alarming; most repeat findings came from cooling logs and sanitizer concentration checks in small independent kitchens preparing for holiday catering.
periods.recommendations: Sustain panel balancing by running a monthly empanelment review and moving low-acuity patients only after direct outreach and language-concordant notice. Target the inspection issue with a December cooling-and-sanitizer mini-campaign, including laminated checklists for the 40 highest-volume holiday caterers. Continue routine inspections on schedule, but add one focused reinspection day for establishments with repeat critical-control-point documentation gaps.

periods.analysis: Primary Care Access Rate increased from 88.3% to 90.1%, a quarter-over-quarter increase of 1.8 percentage points, the strongest access result in this series. Restaurant Inspection Compliance increased from 93.5% to 95.3%, a quarter-over-quarter increase of 1.8 percentage points, again widening the margin above the >=92 target. The January care navigation cohort for residents with diabetes, hypertension, and pregnancy-related needs appears to have improved appointment completion without displacing routine preventive visits. Environmental Health also recovered well after the holiday season, helped by the new digital inspection checklist and faster correction verification through the CivicServe vendor portal.
periods.recommendations: Make the care navigation cohort permanent for high-risk chronic disease and prenatal patients, and add a quarterly review of whether navigation improves completed preventive visits. Keep the CivicServe correction-verification workflow and train all inspectors on photo standards, timestamping, and when an in-person recheck is still required. Use the 90.1% access result as a stretch benchmark while guarding against longer waits for lower-risk residents.

periods.analysis: Primary Care Access Rate decreased from 90.1% to 89.2%, a quarter-over-quarter decrease of 0.9 percentage points, but remains well above the >=85 target. Restaurant Inspection Compliance increased from 95.3% to 96.3%, a quarter-over-quarter increase of 1.0 percentage point, the best inspection result in this eight-quarter arc. The access decrease is a manageable normalization after a very strong Q1 and reflects spring sports physicals, school immunization catch-up, and new resident onboarding in the northeast growth area. The inspection improvement shows that prevention systems are maturing: operators are correcting earlier, inspectors are documenting consistently, and residents are better protected before illness occurs.
periods.recommendations: Sustain access by opening a dedicated school-physical and immunization lane at Westport Clinic from late May through August, separate from chronic-care and prenatal appointments. Extend the digital inspection checklist to temporary-event vendors before the July waterfront festival and require pre-opening self-attestations for refrigeration, handwashing, and allergen labeling. Continue reporting both measures together because clinical access and environmental prevention are complementary parts of Harborview’s health protection system.

periods.analysis: The carried-forward access rate of 89.2% and inspection compliance of 96.3% both exceed target. Access had declined in June amid growth and new-patient demand; neither measure has a new September actual in this slice, so the favorable inspection baseline does not settle the access question.
periods.recommendations: Check September appointment waits and inspection records separately. Preserve new-patient capacity at HV-PC-04 while maintaining the repeat-violation review for food-service operators.
